title: prefix-cache-segmentation-cost-explorer-2026
summary: Exploratory costing sheet that segments traffic by customer cohort and request shape to estimate prefix/KV cache hit elasticity and granular cost savings. Emphasis on small-batch & short-sequence cohorts where prefix cache yields outsized savings.
body:
Purpose:
- Provide a quick-to-run scenario workbook for PM/Eng/Finance to understand where prefix/KV caching delivers most marginal savings across customer cohorts.
- Move beyond a single global hit-rate assumption; show segmentation by sequence length, burstiness, and repetition.

Methodology (high level):
- Split traffic into 6 cohorts (web-chat, mobile-assist, batch-embed, enterprise-high-throughput, low-frequency-api, internal-ci).
- For each cohort, model: requests/day, avg_input_tokens, avg_generated_tokens, baseline_kv_hit (current), candidate_prefix_hit (optimized), and repetition factor (how often similar prefixes repeat).
- Compute token-level savings = (candidate_hit - baseline_hit) * requests/day * avg_generated_tokens. Translate token savings to USD using token_cost_per_1M and to GPU-hours using tokens_per_gpu_hour estimate.
- Run sensitivity slices for +/- 5/10 percentage points in proposed hit rate and for different repetition multipliers.

Assumptions (conservative by default):
- token_cost_per_1M = $1.35 per 1M tokens served (hosted blended).
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = 60,000,000 tokens/hour (inference throughput baseline across fleet for mixed seq lengths).
- Baseline_kv_hit reflects current prefix cache plus microcache: varied per cohort.
- Candidate_prefix_hit assumes implementation of multi-prefix indexing + short-prefix prefetch for 1-3 token prefixes.

Cohort level scenario table (CSV-style) - columns: cohort,requests_per_day,avg_input_tokens,avg_generated_tokens,baseline_kv_hit_pct,candidate_prefix_hit_pct,repetition_factor,effective_savings_tokens_per_day,monthly_cost_savings_usd,monthly_gpu_hours_saved
web-chat,120000,18,40,0.12,0.42,1.6,2304000,$3,110.40,38.40
mobile-assist,80000,12,28,0.09,0.35,1.3,952000,$1,285.20,15.87
batch-embed,15000,0,512,0.03,0.08,1.05,384000,$518.40,6.40
enterprise-high-throughput,25000,10,120,0.20,0.45,2.0,6000000,$8,100.00,100.00
low-frequency-api,10000,6,30,0.05,0.18,1.1,364000,$491.40,6.07
internal-ci,5000,30,5,0.40,0.58,1.0,45000,$60.75,0.75

Notes on table calculations (text):
- effective_savings_tokens_per_day = (candidate_prefix_hit_pct - baseline_kv_hit_pct) * requests_per_day * avg_generated_tokens * repetition_factor
- monthly_cost_savings_usd = effective_savings_tokens_per_day * 30 / 1,000,000 * token_cost_per_1M
- monthly_gpu_hours_saved = (effective_savings_tokens_per_day * 30) / tokens_per_gpu_hour

Key takeaways from this run (draft):
- Enterprise-high-throughput and web-chat cohorts dominate absolute savings; enterprise cohort benefits both from high request volume and strong repetition factor.
- Mobile-assist shows high percentage improvement but middle absolute savings; still impactful for PLG growth cohort cost control.
- Internal-ci and batch-embed are useful optimization pilots because their hit-rate improvements are easier to validate (low noise) though absolute dollar impact is modest.

Sensitivity matrix (text):
- Vary candidate_prefix_hit +/- 5pp and +/- 10pp: observe enterprise-high-throughput monthly savings swing from ~$4.5k to ~$12.1k per 5pp step (calculation in workbook).
- Vary repetition_factor from 1.0 to 2.5: non-linear impact for web-chat where repetition interacts with prefix length distribution.

Micro-experiments recommended (prioritized):
1) Canary short-prefix prefetch on mobile-assist (5% traffic) — easy SDK instrumentation, measure delta in observed early-token cache hits and latency.
2) Enterprise customer pilot: deploy per-tenant indexed-prefix store + monitor cost attribution. Capture telemetry for repeated prefixes at 1,3,5 token lengths.
3) Batch-embed warm-window test: enable KV warm window for 30 minutes and measure hit decay curve (good for validating tokens_per_gpu_hour sensitivity).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How sensitive is tokens_per_gpu_hour to tail latency and sequence length mix? Need a microbench on representative hardware.
- What privacy/compliance guardrails for per-tenant prefix indexing are required for Private deployments? Engage security.
- Operational cost of maintaining prefix index (memory & metadata reads) vs raw token savings — rough rule: hitting rate > 15pp increase needed to justify persistent indexing for small cohorts.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Ethan Brooks: run a 2-week short-prefix canary on mobile-assist, capture prefix hit telemetry (start 2026-05-05).
- Priya Nair: model memory footprint & metadata IOPS for per-tenant index (due 2026-05-12).
- Maya Chen (author): produce a condensed one-pager for Finance with 3 pricing scenarios (conservative/base/optimistic) and expected payback months (due 2026-05-08).

Appendix — quick sensitivity CSV (hit delta by cohort) - columns: cohort,base_candidate_hit,candidate_minus_10pp,candidate_minus_5pp,candidate_plus_5pp,candidate_plus_10pp

Raw hypotheses to validate in telemetry (short bullets):
- Short prefix (1-3 tokens) achieves disproportionate hit uplift in web and mobile chat compared to batch workloads.
- Repetition factor amplifies savings linearly until index saturation / eviction dynamics kick in; measure eviction curve.
- Token-level savings map to reduced GPU-hours only if requests were previously served cold; validate with cold vs warm routing logs.

Editor notes: this is intentionally a lightweight exploratory workbook intended for iterative updates. The exact dollar numbers are placeholders until telemetry-enriched inputs are fed in.
